source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Unauthorized prescribing, because communicating the client’s goals independently changes the medical treatment plan.","B":"Boundary violation, because nurses should not communicate a capable client’s stated preferences to other team members.","C":"Patient advocacy, because the nurse is helping protect the client’s rights, preferences, and participation in care.","D":"Case management only, because advocacy for a client’s wishes is outside the entry-level RN role."}}
source_row.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan identifies advocacy for client rights and needs, interprofessional collaboration, informed consent and plan-of-care activities under Management of Care.
source_row.source_detail: Overview of Content — Management of Care, printed p.7: “Advocate for client rights and needs”; interdisciplinary collaboration and plan-of-care activities. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Management of Care, printed p.7: advocacy/client rights, prioritization, quality improvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, informed consent, legal scope and plan-of-care activities. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client with decision-making capacity says the current care plan does not reflect the client’s goals. The nurse raises the concern during the interprofessional discussion. Which nursing role is demonstrated?
